newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were higher at the end of trade, with the December Confederate bond futures contract still holding ground near the October 9 contract high of 115.80, which was retested again early Monday.
Tuesday's high of 115.54 was hit in midafternoon.
Traders said prices were helped by gains in German bonds, and a favourable tone in U.S. prices.
CS Research was optimistic in its latest weekly report for Swiss bonds, saying that it was keeping its monthly forecast for Swiss 10-year federal bond yields at 3.80 percent 03D05981.
It also said that a recent narrowing in the yield spread between German and Swiss 10-year government bonds was likely due to confidence about European Economic and Monetary Union.
The spread remained narrower than levels seen earlier this fall, but widened slightly from levels seen last week YLDS3.
One trader following domestic bonds said that there was strong turnover, especially in the 2006 to 2008 maturities.
Shorter maturities were mixed, with three-month March EuroSwiss futures on LIFFE ending unchanged and below earlier highs.

There was some speculation among traders watching currencies that the SNB may be near the end of its easing cycle after the mark rose to roughly two-year highs versus the Swiss franc, topping 85.00 centimes.
But one trader at a Swiss bank said that rates have risen on short-dated Swiss paper mainly because of the Swiss franc's latest decline.
Banks selling francs typically borrow the currency short-term before closing positions.
The SNB added liquidity to the Swiss money market earlier on Tuesday.
-- Tuesday prices as follows:
Dec Conf futures up 27 at 115.47.
Dec Comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up 23 at 110.30
Mar Euro Swiss francs unchanged at 97.81.
4-1/2 Apr 2006 bond 104.65/75 yield 3.88 pct
(Monday 104.50/60 yield 3.90)
